_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. My cousin again. Remembers the big one in ’25, Missouri to Indiana in three hours, near seven hundred dead. Says it came out of a cloud that turned. This week, the turning.

replies.say: Where does the turning come from?
replies.back: From the wind, and the storm stands it on end.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions. Tornado country this time.
Funnels and wall clouds, and none of them here, thank God. Next, the storms off the Gulf.
